messages.subject: Combining telemetry and DNA capture
messages.body_plain:
I am attempting to estimate density of deer using DNA data from analysis of deer pellets (scat) as well as telemetry locations. The DNA data are very sparse

> summary(deerDNA)
Object class      capthist
Detector type     count
Detector number   196
Average spacing   100 m
x-range           256671.3 266734.4 m
y-range           4611666 4621977 m
Counts by occasion
                    1 Total
n                  16    16
u                  16    16
f                  16    16
M(t+1)             16    16
losses              0     0
detections         16    16
detectors visited  15    15
detectors used    196   196

However, the telemetry data are not, and none of our collared deer were captured via DNA

> summary(deerTelem)
Object class      capthist
Detector type     telemetry
Number vertices   12
Number polygons   1
Total area        8084.596 ha
x-range           254685 268974 m
y-range           4610869 4620854 m
Counts by occasion
                     1 Total
n                   11    11
u                   11    11
f                   11    11
M(t+1)              11    11
losses               0     0
detections        5678  5678
detectors visited    1     1
detectors used       1     1

Here is the summary of the combined data using the addTelemetry function

> summary(combinedCH)
Object class      capthist
Detector type     count
Detector number   196
Average spacing   100 m
x-range           256671.3 266734.4 m
y-range           4611666 4621977 m
Counts by occasion
                    1 Total
n                  16    16
u                  16    16
f                  16    16
M(t+1)             16    16
losses              0     0
detections         16    16
detectors visited  15    15
detectors used    196   196

11 empty histories
11 telemetered animals, 0 detected
124-1453 locations per animal, mean =  516.18, sd = 375.15

I attempted to run an analysis using the telemetry data to estimate sigma but get the following warnings:

> female.fit <- secr.fit(capthist=combinedCH, CL=TRUE, details=list(telemetrysigma=TRUE), detectfn="HHN",
+                        buffer=1000, mask=areaextent, method="Nelder-Mead", binomN=0)
Checking data
Preparing detection design matrices
Finding initial parameter values...
Warning messages:
1: In updatemodel(model, detectfn, 14:18, "g0", "lambda0") :
  replacing g0 by lambda0 in model for detectfn 14
2: In autoini(ch, msk, binomN = details$binomN, ignoreusage = details$ignoreusage) :
  could not calculate 'dbar'; using detector spacing
3: In secr.fit(capthist = combinedCH, CL = TRUE, details = list(telemetrysigma = TRUE),  :
  'secr.fit' failed because initial values not found (data sparse?); specify transformed values in 'start'
>

Do you see any problems with my coding? I have tried different buffer sizes, with/without a mask, details$telemetrybvn = TRUE, and the same errors arise.

Starting values of D = log(0.01), g0 = log(100) to log(100000), and sigma=log(300) to log(10000) don't help.

Any suggestions for starting values to try?  Deer density is about 0.07 deer/ha, home range size is about 300 ha.

Thanks,

Duane

messages.subject: Re: SECR training workshops
messages.body_plain:
Greeting SECR list

A follow-up to Prof. Borchers' February message.  The workshop taking place in Seattle later this month is filled.

Places are still available on the 3-day workshop taking place in St Andrews 29-31 August 2016.

We hope to attract ecologists intending to use spatial capture-recapture methods in their work estimating animal abundance and distribution.  The workshop will be 'hands on' using R (with which we assume participants have some familiarity).  Along with exercises, we encourage participants to bring their own data formatted in accordance with secr or admbsecr package specifications.

More information regarding the workshop along with registration details can be found at this link:

http://creem2.st-andrews.ac.uk/spatial-capture-recapture-workshop-29-31-august-2016/ <http://www.google.com/url?q=http%3A%2F%2Fcreem2.st-andrews.ac.uk%2Fspatial-capture-recapture-workshop-29-31-august-2016%2F&sa=D&sntz=1&usg=AFQjCNF9zUNNTc3C0tJwWW24XHWBQ45w0A>

On Tuesday, February 23, 2016 at 5:15:47 PM UTC, David Borchers wrote:
>
> I and colleagues from the University of St Andrews will be putting on a 3-day SECR workshop in St Andrews, Scotland, in August, and a one-day SECR workshop attached to the ISEC conference in Seattle in June. Deatils below.
>
>
> Instructors: David Borchers, Ben Stevenson (Seattle & St Andrews) and Eric Rexstad (St Andrews only)
>
>
> Content: The workshops have overlapping content, but different duration (hence intensity), with the St Andrews workshop including analyses of participants' own data, and the Seattle workshop involving example datasets only.
>
>
>
> The workshops will cover the key concepts underlying SECR methods, and provide training in use of the methods. They will cover binary, count and time-to-detection data types, and all kinds of detectors, including camera traps, hair snares, acoustic detectors, mist nets and single-catch traps, and transect and area searches. Participants will get hands-on training in estimating density, abundance and related parameters.  Issues of measures of precision and model selection will be discussed.  Use of SECR with spatially-referenced variables for generating predictions of animal density and habitat use across landscapes will be covered.
>
>
>
> Training workshop in Seattle 26 June 2016.  One day workshop held immediately prior to the International Statistical Ecology Conference on the campus of the University of Washington.  The workshop will introduce participants to SECR methods ranging from the most basic to the most recently developed.  Some example analyses (using R) will be conducted during the workshop.
>
>
>
> Further information and registration details for Seattle workshop can be found at
>
> http://depts.washington.edu/uwconf/wordpress/isec2016/workshops/
>
>
>
> Training workshop in St Andrews 29-31 August 2016.  Target audience is biologists/ecologists who intend to, or are currently using spatial capture-recapture methods for the estimation of abundance/density/distribution.  The workshop will be hands-on, primarily using the R package 'secr', although mention will be made of other software.  Participants are encouraged to bring their own data formatted for use by 'secr' or 'admbsecr' (primarily for acoustic data). Familiarity with the R language is assumed and will be aided with pre-workshop online tutorials.
>
>
>
> Further information and registration details for St Andrews workshop can be found at
> http://creem2.st-andrews.ac.uk/spatial-capture-recapture-workshop-29-31-august-2016/

messages.subject: trap happy/shy
messages.body_plain:
Hi everyone,
I have been using the secr package in R and have found the best model using the AIC comparison to be the behavioral response to a site. I would like to check if this response is positive or negative, but I am not sure what I need to compare to show this, can you point me in the right direction? I would appreciate it!
Kind regards
Tara

messages.subject: Re: trap happy/shy
messages.body_plain:
Tara
The direction of the response is shown by the beta coefficient for g0.bkTRUE (see for example the table of beta parameter values that is displayed when you print a fitted model object). Positive values indicate a positive response. For estimates of the two levels of the real parameter use predict(fittedmodel, newdata=data.frame(bk=0:1)) where bk=0 corresponds to the naive state.
Murray

messages.subject: Re: Combining telemetry and DNA capture
messages.body_plain:
Hi Duane

Sorry for the delay - as you know, this went in the 'too hard' pile for a few days. I know that weakly documented implementation of combined telemetry & SECR is temperamental, and I thought you might be a hapless victim, but perhaps the problem is more basic.

Your code looks impeccable except possibly for the starting values for which you didn't show the code (obviously you should specify lambda0 not  g0 for detectfn = 'HHN', which is definitely the detectfn to use).

It must be a worry that there are no DNA recaptures (as I read the summary) and no overlap between the telemetry animals and the DNA sample. That seems to mean that you have a 'no recapture' dataset overall, hence no means to estimate lambda0 and D.

For the telemetered animals you will get an estimate of the pooled sigma essentially without error just by applying RPSV(telemCH, CC=TRUE) to the telemetry part of the dataset. That can be used as a fixed input for analysing the DNA histories (fixed = list(sigma = XXX)) but without recaptures I don't see that lambda0 is going to be identifiable.

Murray
